subject: Post-demo: streaming SLO clarification & customer-led k6 run coordination
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Tim Bradley <tim.bradley@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: streaming SLO clarification & customer-led k6 run coordination

Tim — thanks for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the customer-led load run: 

Summary of what we discussed:
- Goal: validate streaming concurrency and end-to-end latency SLOs for the new Acme voice-transcription flow.
- Redwood will provide a k6 starter script and a runbook template. Customer will run from their load cluster (k6 / Locust) and whitelist Redwood endpoints.
- Key metrics to confirm during the run: first-token latency (p50/p95), sustained throughput (RPS), concurrent streaming sessions, and 99th pct tail.

Action items (proposed):
1) Customer to confirm target traffic profile (RPS, concurrency, session duration) — can you confirm numbers below?
2) Customer to provide test window(s) and list of source IPs for allowlist.
3) We’ll share k6 starter + runbook and a temp test account with scoped API key.
4) Redwood to stand up an observer for metrics (traces + token-level cost estimate) during the run and be on-call for failures.

I’ve attached a k6 starter and the runbook template to this thread. If the numbers you want to validate are different than what we discussed, flag them and we’ll adjust the script.

Proposed default profile (please confirm):
- Sustained throughput: 150 RPS (burst to 300 RPS for short spikes)
- Streaming concurrency: 400 concurrent streams (average session 45s)
- Acceptable SLOs: first-token p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms; end-to-end median < 200ms (for single-turn streaming).

Preferred test window: Nov 16–17 09:00–13:00 PT (two 2-hour windows with a short warm-up). If that doesn’t work for you, propose alternatives.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- acme-k6-starter.js (script stub)
- redwood-runbook-template.pdf (runbook template)

From: Tim Bradley <tim.bradley@acmehealth.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health SRE <sre-team@acmehealth.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 18:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming SLO clarification & customer-led k6 run coordination

Thanks Jasmine — clear notes, appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side after the internal sync: 

Confirmed targets we want to validate in the run: 
- Sustained throughput: 200 RPS (we’ll plan for 20% margin, so script should be able to ramp to 240 RPS).
- Streaming concurrency: target 500 concurrent active sessions (typical session ~60s, some up to 2m).
- Latency SLOs: first-token p95 target <= 250ms; p99 target <= 600ms. End-to-end p95 <= 400ms for transcription payloads up to ~3s audio.
- Error budget: less than 1.5% failed requests for the whole window.

We can run November 18 08:00–12:00 PT (reserve four hours — we’ll probably do two 90m runs with a warm-up). Please provide the temp API key and the exact endpoint hostname so we can add to our routing.

IP allowlist: we’ll whitelist the following egress CIDRs from our load cluster: 34.208.120.0/24, 34.208.121.0/24. If Redwood needs narrower IPs per-region let us know.

One more ask: can Redwood include a version of the k6 script that sends a small preflight payload (1–2s audio) to validate correct auth and payload decoding before the ramp? That will speed up our dry run.

—Tim
Tim Bradley
Lead SRE, Acme Health
tim.bradley@acmehealth.io

Tim / team — copying a couple of operational details so we can finalize logistics: 

1) Temp test credentials: we will provision a scoped API key that only allows the /v1/stream endpoint and will expire after 48 hours. Expect to receive the key by EOD Nov 11.

2) Endpoint hostnames: streaming.redwood-prod-west-1.redwood.com (use TLS, mTLS optional). If your egress requires region-specific endpoints we can provide per-az targets.

3) Preflight script: attaching a tiny preflight snippet in the acme-k6-starter.js we sent — it runs a short 1–2s payload and asserts 200 response + valid token header.

4) Observability: Marissa will be on-call to correlate traces during the run; we’ll provide a live dashboard (tokenized) and a short post-run artifact with p50/p95/p99 for first-token and full-response.

Ben Carter

Tim — thanks, that all sounds good. Two quick operational notes and confirmations before we lock the window: 

- We’ll provision the API key on Nov 11 (Ben), and will share the key via our secure secret transfer link (one-time access). Please confirm the recipient email that should receive it.

- Observability link: I’ve created a temporary dashboard and shared it in the Drive folder (read-only) — link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Aabcdefg12345. We’ll post a short run checklist in the runbook (warm-up, steady-state, cool-down).

Proposed final schedule: Nov 18 08:00–12:00 PT with two runs: 08:15–09:45 (dry + warm-up to 150 RPS), 10:15–11:45 (full ramp to 240 RPS / 500 concurrency). Please confirm and we’ll lock calendars and the allowlist.

If you want us on the call for both runs we can join on the first full run (10:15) and remain reachable for the second.

Thanks —
